```text
# #3606: Patch (part 2 of 6): the desktop sheds load too: a slow frame window steps the shed ladder on every viewport
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What it does

Part of #3604. The effects director already watches frame times and, on a slow window, sheds one stage deeper: motes, then far auras, then the moving faces furthest from the pointer, never a set piece's main beats (R3351000, `fx/shed.ts`, `fx/director.ts`). But only a phone director publishes stages past full: `options.phone` gates `setShedLevel` (`director.ts:56`, `:91`, `:225`), and "a desktop director never sheds". A laptop with a weak GPU, or a desktop at a high refresh rate, keeps every layer running however slow it gets.

Let every viewport's director publish shed stages on slow windows, keeping the same ruled order, the same recovery (`FX_ADAPT_RECOVER_WINDOWS`) and the same slow test (`FX_ADAPT_SLOW_MS`, `FX_ADAPT_SLOW_FACTOR` × refresh). The phone keeps its tighter per-layer budgets (`PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET`, the phone particle cap). Only the "never sheds on desktop" rule goes. If a desktop-specific threshold is needed so a healthy desktop never sheds, it is a named constant beside the phone's.

This changes what R3351000 says. Edit its note (`spec/rulings/R3351000.md`) and add a ruling from this issue's block for the desktop behaviour, as CLAUDE.md rule 3 says, its proving test named after it.

### Acceptance

- A director built without `phone` publishes `SHED_MOTES`, then `SHED_AURAS`, then `SHED_FACES` across consecutive slow windows, and steps back to `SHED_FULL` after the recovery windows. Unit test in `fx/director.test.ts` / `fx/shed.test.ts`, named after the new ruling.
- A healthy desktop (frames at the display's refresh) never leaves `SHED_FULL`.
- A set piece's main beats still play at every stage, as on the phone today.
- The motion slots (`cards/motionSlots.ts`) and aura layers react to a desktop shed exactly as to a phone one.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

### Blocked by, part of

Part of #3604

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42883290694)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Every viewport's effects director publishes shed stages on slow frame windows, not only a phone director's. A desktop director steps `SHED_FULL → SHED_MOTES → SHED_AURAS → SHED_FACES` on consecutive slow windows and back down over `FX_ADAPT_RECOVER_WINDOWS` healthy windows, using the same ruled order, recovery, and slow test (`FX_ADAPT_SLOW_MS`, `FX_ADAPT_SLOW_FACTOR` × refresh) as the phone. The phone keeps its tighter per-layer budgets (`PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET`, the phone particle cap); only the "never sheds on desktop" rule goes. This amends `R3351000` and adds ruling `R3606000` (first free number in issue 3606's block, verified free) with its proving test.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/fx/director.ts` | change | Remove `phone` from `FxDirectorOptions`, the `const phone` line, and the `if (phone)` gate on `setShedLevel` in `adapt`; rewrite the option doc, the `shedLevel()` doc, and the slow-window comment |
| `apps/web/src/fx/FxLayer.tsx` | change | Delete the `phone:` line of the `createFxDirector` call |
| `apps/web/src/routes/dev/fx.tsx` | change | Delete the `phone:` line of the `createFxDirector` call |
| `apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx` | change | Delete the `phone:` line of the `createFxDirector` call |
| `apps/web/src/stats/StatShowcase.tsx` | change | Delete the `phone:` line of the `createFxDirector` call |
| `apps/web/src/fx/shed.ts` | change | Header comment: the shed order applies on every viewport, not only the phone |
| `apps/web/src/fx/director.test.ts` | change | Drop `{ phone: true }` from harnesses; rewrite the desktop-never-sheds test; add `R3606000` desktop tests |
| `spec/rulings/R3351000.md` | change | Body: the adaptive cap of every viewport's director sheds in the ruled order; desktop keeps the phone's budgets out |
| `spec/rulings/R3606000.md` | new | The desktop-shed ruling note with front matter |
| `spec/pending/3606.md` | new | The §11 paragraph for `R3606000` |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`; any `crates/` or `e2e/` file; `apps/web/src/cards/motionSlots.ts`, `apps/web/src/fx/aura/AuraLayer.tsx`, `apps/web/src/fx/aura/TileAura.tsx` (they read the viewport-blind shared `shed.ts`, so they follow a desktop shed with no edit); `apps/web/src/fx/constants.ts` (no new constant; decided below). Governing spec: `spec/10-engine-guide.md` §10.10 presentation-only boundary, rulings `R200`, `R2785000`, `R3351000`.

## Steps

1. `apps/web/src/fx/director.ts`, `createFxDirector`: delete `const phone = options.phone ?? false;` and change `if (phone) setShedLevel(shedStage() + 1);` to `setShedLevel(shedStage() + 1);`. Recovery (`setShedLevel(shedStage() - 1)`) is already ungated and stays as is.
2. Same file, `FxDirectorOptions`: delete the `phone?: boolean` field and its doc comment. Delete or rewrite the `shedLevel()` doc sentence "Only a phone director publishes stages past full (`phone`); a desktop director never sheds." to "Every viewport's director publishes stages past full on slow windows (`R3606000`)." Rewrite the slow-window comment to drop "on a phone" and the "Desktop keeps the cap halving without shedding" sentence.
3. `apps/web/src/fx/FxLayer.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/dev/fx.tsx`, `apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx`, `apps/web/src/stats/StatShowcase.tsx`: delete each `phone: ... < FX_MOBILE_WIDTH` line. In each file, if the `FX_MOBILE_WIDTH` import is then unused (check; `FxLayer.tsx` still uses it for `compact`), delete it from the import. TypeScript enforces completeness: any leftover `phone:` line is a type error.
4. `apps/web/src/fx/shed.ts`: rewrite the header comment's "On a phone" scoping to every viewport (order, pointer rule, and "never a set piece's main beats" stay word for word).
5. `apps/web/src/fx/director.test.ts`: remove `{ phone: true }` from every `harness(...)` call in the `R3351000` shed-order describe block (behavior is now identical, so the order, beats, dispose, and idle-recovery tests prove both viewports unchanged). Rewrite the test at old line 885 (`a desktop director halves its cap on slow windows but never sheds`) as `it("R3606000 a desktop director sheds motes, then far auras, then faces, and recovers one stage per healthy run", ...)`: default harness, `settleOn60Hz` shape, three slow `trip` runs asserting levels 1, 2, 3, then three `FX_ADAPT_WINDOW * FX_ADAPT_RECOVER_WINDOWS` healthy runs asserting 2, 1, 0 (copy the phone test's `trip`/`settled` helpers at lines 781–787).
6. Same file, add `it("R3606000 healthy desktop frames at the display's refresh never leave full", ...)`: default harness, 16 ms frames for `FX_ADAPT_WINDOW * 5`, assert `shedLevel()` 0 and capacity untouched. Add `it("R3606000 a desktop shed still plays a set piece's main beats", ...)`: shed to 3 via slow windows, play takeover, setPiece, launch, rift, anomalyTitle, assert each mounts (copy the `TINT` block and cue list from the phone beats test).
7. `spec/rulings/R3606000.md`: new note, front matter `id: R3606000`, title naming the desktop shed question, `cards: "§10.10; R200, R2785000, R3351000, issue #3606"`, `proven_in: [apps/web/src/fx/director.test.ts]`; body: every viewport's director sheds in `R3351000`'s order on the same slow test and recovery; the phone keeps `PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET` and the phone particle cap; healthy frames at refresh never shed; set pieces' beats still mount at every stage. Every ruling named as `[[R…]]`, every section as `[[§…]]`.
8. `spec/rulings/R3351000.md`: edit the "One shared budget" paragraph's "`FX_ADAPT_*`, the phone director" scoping to every viewport's director; add `R3606000` to `cards`. Leave the phone budgets, frame numbers, and rejected list alone.
9. `spec/pending/3606.md`: new file with the one §11 paragraph: `**[[R3606000]] … (issue #3606, 2026-11-10)**: …` in the style of `spec/pending/3350.md`.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/fx/director.test.ts`: `it("R3606000 a desktop director sheds motes, then far auras, then faces, and recovers one stage per healthy run")` asserts levels 1/2/3 across three slow windows, clamp at 3, then 2/1/0 across three healthy runs; `it("R3606000 healthy desktop frames at the display's refresh never leave full")` asserts level 0 after sustained 16 ms frames; `it("R3606000 a desktop shed still plays a set piece's main beats")` asserts all five DOM beats mount at stage 3. Existing `R3351000` phone tests (rewritten without `phone: true`) assert the order, emission halving, recovery, dispose reset, and idle recovery are unchanged. Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/fx/director.test.ts`.
- `apps/web/src/fx/shed.test.ts`: unchanged; run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/fx/shed.test.ts` to confirm the shared scales are untouched.
- Motion-slot and aura reaction to a desktop shed needs no new test: `apps/web/src/cards/motionSlots.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/fx/aura/AuraLayer.test.tsx`, `apps/web/src/fx/aura/TileAura.test.tsx` already prove reaction to the shared shed level, which is viewport-blind; run the motionSlots and aura test files they name.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` (catches leftover `phone:` lines and unused imports), then `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] A default (desktop) director publishes 1, 2, 3 across slow windows and recovers 2, 1, 0 over healthy runs; healthy 16 ms frames never leave 0
- [ ] Set pieces' main beats mount at desktop stage 3; mote emission still halves with a one-mote floor
- [ ] No `phone` reference remains in `director.ts` or any call site; typecheck green
- [ ] `R3351000.md` edited, `R3606000.md` and `spec/pending/3606.md` added, `proven_in` listing the test file
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/fx/director.test.ts`, the shed, motionSlots, and aura test files, typecheck, and `cargo jackioh spec check` all pass

## Risks

- The old desktop-never-sheds test contradicts the new rule; rewriting (not deleting) it keeps coverage while the `R3351000` edit authorizes the change.
- `shed.ts` level is module-shared across directors: existing dispose-reset and `afterEach(resetShedForTests())` behavior already prevents cross-test leaks; the new desktop tests rely on the same seam.
- Removing the `phone` option changes a public factory signature; the four call sites are all in-tree and compiler-checked, and no test constructs with `phone` after step 5.
- Presentation-only boundary holds: `adapt` still reads only frame times, `shed.ts` readers only the level and pointer, no game state involved.

## Open questions

None. Decided in-plan: no desktop-specific threshold constant is needed, because the existing slow test already clears a healthy desktop (30 healthy 60 Hz frames sum to ~501 ms against a ~720 ms trip line, with wider margins at higher refresh rates), so the "named constant beside the phone's" clause does not trigger; if CI's frame probe later shows a healthy desktop shedding, that is a new issue with its own ruling, not part of this change.
```
